entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married and was found hanging on 19.03.2023.
The allegations were levelled against the entire family members.
3. The Counsel for the applicants has filed a supplementary affidavit bringing on record the statement of the informant who has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution story.
The supplementary affidavit is taken on record.
The applicants are the father-in-law and the mother-in-law of the victim and no specific allegations have been levelled against the applicant.
The applicants are in custody since 10.04.2023.

sentences.text: 4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the fact that the informant has turned hostile as is clear from the supplementary affidavit and the applicants have no criminal antecedents and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicants if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicants are entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicants Anju and Munendra Tyagi @ Sonu be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.124 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of the DP Act, Police Station Kharkhauda, District Meerut on their furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicants shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicants shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which they are accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
